title: Virtual Machine Scale Sets and automatic scaling

videos.script: A shop with three servers needs five at lunchtime, and three again at night. {{count}} This lesson is about the thing that holds that number. A scale set is a model of one machine, and a count. Azure makes machines from the model until the count is met. {{model}} You will write one in Bicep for the shop's order API. Three instances, three zones, behind the load balancer. And you will compile it on your laptop, with no Azure account. {{compile}} Then a second resource moves the count. An autoscale rule reads the CPU once a minute. It averages ten minutes of readings, and only then does it act. You will work out, minute by minute, when lunchtime adds two machines. And why a short cooldown would add two more. {{window}} The compiler checks the shape of all this, but not everything. It catches one mistake and lets two through, and the lesson shows all three. {{mistakes}} Last comes health. A scale set that cannot tell a broken machine from a good one cannot upgrade safely, and cannot repair anything. {{health}}
